newsitem.title: CANADA: Farm output led Manitoba to 3rd year of GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Farm output led Manitoba to 3rd year of GDP growth.

text.p: Growing agricultural output and more exports were credited on Monday for Manitoba's third consecutive year of growth in real gross domestic product, Manitoba Industry Minister Jim Downey said in a statement.

"A surge in the agricultural sector provided much of the push, aided by continuing strength in exports, strong personal income growth, increased manufacturing, greater consumer spending and high levels of business investment," Downey said.
Manitoba posted growth in real GDP of 2.9 percent in 1996, second only to Saskatchewan's 3.3 percent, but ahead of Canada's 1.5 percent.
Total exports rose 9.3 percent, or C$1.1 billion compared to Canada's increase of 3.5 percent.
Manitoba business investment was the best of any province with growth of 15.5 percent, or C$490 million, twice the national rate of growth of 7.8 percent.
Farm income recovered from a net loss of C$26 million in 1995 to a net gain of C$525 million in 1996, Downey said.
Farm income produced a total personal income growth of 4.7 percent compared to Canada's average of two percent.
Personal disposable income after taxes rose 4.4 person pronvince-wide in 1996, four times the national average.
